questions.text: Which muscle inserts into the medial lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus?
questions.correctAnswer: C. Teres major
questions.explanation: Teres major inserts into the medial lip of the bicipital groove. Pectoralis major inserts into the lateral lip, while latissimus dorsi inserts into the floor of the groove ("a lady between two majors").

questions.text: The clavicular head of the pectoralis major originates from which part of the clavicle?
options: Lateral one-third of the superior surface
Medial half of the anterior border
Inferior surface of the middle third
questions.correctAnswer: B. Medial half of the anterior border
questions.explanation: The clavicular head of pectoralis major arises from the anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle, whereas the sternocostal head arises from the anterior manubrium, sternal body, and upper six costal cartilages.

questions.text: Which muscle inserts into the medial border of the coracoid process of the scapula?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Pectoralis minor
questions.explanation: Pectoralis minor inserts onto the medial border and superior surface of the coracoid process. In contrast, coracobrachialis and the short head of biceps brachii originate from its apex.

questions.text: The tendon of latissimus dorsi inserts into which bony landmark of the humerus?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Floor of the intertubercular groove
questions.explanation: Latissimus dorsi winds around the lower border of teres major to insert into the floor of the intertubercular groove of the humerus.

questions.text: Paralysis of which muscle produces characteristic "winging of the scapula" due to long thoracic nerve injury?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Serratus anterior
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior anchors the costal surface of the medial border and inferior angle of the scapula against the thoracic wall. Injury to the long thoracic nerve (C5, C6, C7) causes the medial border to lift posteriorly off the thorax.

questions.text: Which rotator cuff muscle inserts onto the lesser tubercle of the humerus?
questions.correctAnswer: D. Subscapularis
questions.explanation: Subscapularis is the only anterior rotator cuff muscle and the sole rotator cuff muscle inserting on the lesser tubercle. Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and teres minor insert onto the facets of the greater tubercle.

questions.text: What is the precise sequential insertion of muscles on the three facets of the greater tubercle of the humerus, from superior to inferior?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Supraspinatus, Infraspinatus, Teres minor
questions.explanation: The greater tubercle of the humerus displays three muscular facets on its posterosuperior surface: superior facet (supraspinatus), middle facet (infraspinatus), and inferior facet (teres minor).

questions.text: Which muscle initiates the first 0 to 15 degrees of abduction of the arm at the glenohumeral joint?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Supraspinatus
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus initiates abduction of the humerus (0-15 degrees) by seating the humeral head firmly against the glenoid cavity, after which the multipennate central fibers of the deltoid take over (15-90 degrees).

questions.text: The multipennate central fibers of the deltoid muscle originate from which bony structure?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Lateral border of the acromion
questions.explanation: The acromial (intermediate) part of the deltoid is multipennate to maximize contractile power and originates from the lateral border of the acromion process.

questions.text: Which muscle is innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve (C5)?
questions.correctAnswer: A. Rhomboid major
questions.explanation: The dorsal scapular nerve originates from the C5 root of the brachial plexus and descends along the medial border of the scapula to supply rhomboid major, rhomboid minor, and levator scapulae.

questions.text: Teres major receives its motor innervation from the:
questions.correctAnswer: C. Lower subscapular nerve
questions.explanation: Teres major is innervated specifically by the lower subscapular nerve (C5, C6) arising from the posterior cord. The upper subscapular nerve supplies only subscapularis.

questions.text: Which muscle inserts into the clavicle in the subclavian groove on its inferior surface?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Subclavius
questions.explanation: Subclavius originates at the junction of the first rib and its costal cartilage and inserts into the subclavian groove on the inferior surface of the clavicular shaft.

questions.text: Which nerve innervates both the supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Suprascapular nerve
questions.explanation: The suprascapular nerve (C5, C6 from the superior trunk) runs under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa to supply supraspinatus, then winds around the spinoglenoid notch to supply infraspinatus.

questions.text: The nerve supply of the teres minor muscle is derived from the:
questions.correctAnswer: B. Axillary nerve
questions.explanation: The posterior terminal division of the axillary nerve supplies teres minor (distinguished histologically by a pseudoganglion) and continues as the upper lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm.

questions.text: Which muscle forms the anterior boundary of the axilla (anterior axillary fold)?
questions.correctAnswer: C. Pectoralis major
questions.explanation: The lower rounded border of the pectoralis major muscle forms the anterior axillary fold.

questions.text: Which pair of muscles forms the posterior axillary fold?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Latissimus dorsi and teres major
questions.explanation: The posterior axillary fold is formed by the tendon of latissimus dorsi sweeping anteriorly around the lower border of teres major.

questions.text: Serratus anterior inserts along which part of the scapula?
options: Entire length of the costal aspect of the medial border
Superior border medial to the notch
questions.correctAnswer: B. Entire length of the costal aspect of the medial border
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior inserts continuously along the anterior/costal lip of the medial border of the scapula, concentrating heavily at the inferior angle.

questions.text: Which muscle is responsible for both adduction and medial rotation of the arm at the glenohumeral joint?
questions.correctAnswer: C. Teres major
questions.explanation: Teres major adducts, medially rotates, and extends the humerus. Infraspinatus and teres minor are lateral rotators.

questions.text: The subscapularis muscle is innervated by which nerves?
questions.correctAnswer: A. Upper and lower subscapular nerves
questions.explanation: Subscapularis receives both upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5, C6) arising from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus.

questions.text: The primary action of the subscapularis muscle on the humerus is:
questions.correctAnswer: B. Medial rotation
questions.explanation: Arising from the anterior subscapular fossa and inserting onto the lesser tubercle, subscapularis acts as a powerful medial (internal) rotator of the arm.

questions.text: Which muscle passes through the triangular space and separates teres minor from teres major?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Long head of triceps brachii
questions.explanation: The long head of triceps descends from the infraglenoid tubercle between teres minor superiorly and teres major inferiorly, dividing the interval into quadrangular and triangular spaces.

questions.text: Trapezius receives its motor innervation from the:
questions.correctAnswer: B. Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI)
questions.explanation: The spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) provides motor innervation to the trapezius, whereas cervical nerves C3 and C4 supply sensory proprioception.

questions.text: Which rotator cuff tendon is most susceptible to impingement under the coracoacromial arch?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Supraspinatus
questions.explanation: The supraspinatus tendon travels beneath the coracoacromial arch (acromion, coracoid process, and coracoacromial ligament), making it vulnerable to subacromial friction and tears.

questions.text: Levator scapulae inserts into the:
options: Medial border of the scapula between superior angle and spine
questions.correctAnswer: A. Medial border of the scapula between superior angle and spine
questions.explanation: Levator scapulae originates from the transverse processes of C1-C4 and inserts onto the dorsal surface of the medial border of the scapula between the superior angle and the triangular root of the spine.

questions.text: The clavipectoral fascia is pierced by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.correctAnswer: D. Medial pectoral nerve
questions.explanation: The clavipectoral fascia is pierced by the cephalic vein, thoracoacromial artery, lateral pectoral nerve, and lymphatic vessels. The medial pectoral nerve pierces pectoralis minor directly.

questions.text: Which muscle is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Coracobrachialis
questions.explanation: The musculocutaneous nerve leaves the lateral cord of the brachial plexus and enters the arm by piercing coracobrachialis.

questions.text: The long head of the biceps brachii originates from which bony landmark?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula
questions.explanation: The long head of biceps originates from the supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and the glenoid labrum, traveling intracapsularly across the humeral head.

questions.text: The short head of the biceps brachii arises conjointly with which muscle from the apex of the coracoid process?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Coracobrachialis
questions.explanation: The short head of biceps brachii and coracobrachialis arise together from the tip of the coracoid process of the scapula via a common conjoined tendon.

questions.text: Biceps brachii inserts primarily into the:
options: Rough posterior part of the radial tuberosity
questions.correctAnswer: B. Rough posterior part of the radial tuberosity
questions.explanation: The tendon of the biceps brachii twists and inserts into the rough posterior aspect of the radial tuberosity, separated from the smooth anterior portion by a bursa.

questions.text: The bicipital aponeurosis extends medially from the biceps tendon to blend with the:
options: Antebrachial deep fascia over the common flexor group
questions.correctAnswer: A. Antebrachial deep fascia over the common flexor group
questions.explanation: The bicipital aponeurosis (lacertus fibrosus) passes medially across the brachial artery and median nerve to blend with the deep fascia of the anterior forearm.

questions.text: Which muscle is the chief (primary) flexor of the elbow joint in all positions of forearm rotation?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Brachialis
questions.explanation: Brachialis inserts onto the ulna (coronoid process and tuberosity); because the ulna does not rotate during pronation/supination, brachialis acts as the workhorse elbow flexor in all forearm postures.

questions.text: The brachialis muscle receives dual innervation from which two nerves?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Musculocutaneous nerve and radial nerve
questions.explanation: Brachialis is supplied medially by the musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6) and receives proprioceptive and motor innervation to its inferolateral border from the radial nerve (C7).

questions.text: Coracobrachialis inserts into which site?
options: Mid-portion of the medial border and surface of the humeral shaft
questions.correctAnswer: B. Mid-portion of the medial border and surface of the humeral shaft
questions.explanation: Coracobrachialis inserts into a linear impression on the medial border of the humeral shaft near its midpoint, opposite the deltoid tuberosity.

questions.text: The long head of the triceps brachii originates from the:
options: Posterior humeral shaft superior to the radial groove
questions.correctAnswer: B. Infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula
questions.explanation: The long head of triceps brachii originates from the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula.

questions.text: The lateral head of triceps brachii arises from the:
options: Posterior surface of the humerus superior and lateral to the radial groove
Posterior surface of the humerus inferior and medial to the radial groove
questions.correctAnswer: B. Posterior surface of the humerus superior and lateral to the radial groove
questions.explanation: The lateral head of triceps originates from the posterior surface of the humerus superior and lateral to the radial (spiral) groove.

questions.text: The medial head of the triceps brachii arises from the:
options: Posterior surface of the humerus inferior and medial to the radial groove
questions.correctAnswer: A. Posterior surface of the humerus inferior and medial to the radial groove
questions.explanation: The medial head originates from the expansive posterior surface of the humeral shaft inferior and medial to the radial groove and from both intermuscular septa.

questions.text: All three heads of the triceps brachii insert into which anatomical landmark?
options: Superior surface of the olecranon process of the ulna
questions.correctAnswer: B. Superior surface of the olecranon process of the ulna
questions.explanation: All three heads of triceps unite into a single tendon that inserts into the posterior aspect of the superior surface of the ulnar olecranon.

questions.text: The anconeus muscle is innervated by a branch from the:
options: Radial nerve (nerve to anconeus via radial nerve in spiral groove)
questions.correctAnswer: B. Radial nerve (nerve to anconeus via radial nerve in spiral groove)
questions.explanation: Anconeus is innervated by a dedicated branch of the radial nerve that arises in the spiral groove and travels through the medial head of triceps.

questions.text: The anconeus muscle originates from the:
options: Posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus
questions.correctAnswer: B. Posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus
questions.explanation: Anconeus originates from the posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus.

questions.text: Anconeus inserts into the:
options: Lateral surface of the olecranon and superior quarter of the posterior ulna
questions.correctAnswer: A. Lateral surface of the olecranon and superior quarter of the posterior ulna
questions.explanation: Anconeus inserts into the lateral aspect of the olecranon and the upper posterior shaft of the ulna, assisting in terminal elbow extension and stabilizing the joint.

questions.text: Which head of the triceps brachii acts across two joints (glenohumeral and elbow)?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Long head
questions.explanation: Because it originates from the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula, only the long head crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints.

questions.text: In a fracture through the radial groove of the humerus, which muscle head is typically spared because its nerve branch arises proximal to the groove?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Long head of triceps
questions.explanation: Nerve branches to the long head leave the radial nerve high in the axilla proximal to the spiral groove, leaving long head contraction intact during midshaft fractures.

questions.text: Which muscle acts as the most powerful supinator of the flexed forearm?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Biceps brachii
questions.explanation: When the elbow is flexed to 90 degrees, the pull of biceps brachii on the radial tuberosity creates maximal mechanical leverage for rapid, forceful supination.

questions.text: Brachialis inserts into the:
options: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
questions.correctAnswer: B. Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
questions.explanation: Brachialis inserts into the anterior surface of the coronoid process and the rough tuberosity of the ulna.

questions.text: The functional role of the coracobrachialis is primarily:
options: Extension and abduction of the arm
Flexion and weak adduction of the arm at the glenohumeral joint
questions.correctAnswer: B. Flexion and weak adduction of the arm at the glenohumeral joint
questions.explanation: Coracobrachialis assists pectoralis major and anterior deltoid in arm flexion and adduction, and helps resist downward dislocation of the humeral head.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT part of the superficial group of anterior forearm muscles arising from the common flexor origin?
questions.correctAnswer: C. Flexor digitorum profundus
questions.explanation: Flexor digitorum profundus belongs to the deep flexor layer. The superficial flexor group consists of pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, and flexor carpi ulnaris.

questions.text: The common flexor tendon originates from which humeral landmark?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Medial epicondyle
questions.explanation: The common flexor tendon attaches to the anterior aspect of the medial epicondyle of the humerus.

questions.text: The median nerve passes between the two heads of origin of which muscle?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Pronator teres
questions.explanation: The median nerve enters the forearm between the humeral and ulnar heads of pronator teres.

questions.text: Pronator teres inserts into the:
options: Roughened impression on the middle of the lateral surface of the radial shaft
Anterior surface of the distal ulna
questions.correctAnswer: B. Roughened impression on the middle of the lateral surface of the radial shaft
questions.explanation: Pronator teres inserts onto the middle of the lateral surface of the radial shaft at the point of maximum radial curvature.

questions.text: Flexor carpi radialis inserts into the base of which metacarpal bones?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals
questions.explanation: Flexor carpi radialis inserts onto the anterior (palmar) bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals.

questions.text: Palmaris longus tendon passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum to insert into the:
questions.correctAnswer: B. Palmar aponeurosis
questions.explanation: Palmaris longus crosses superficial to the flexor retinaculum and inserts into the central palmar aponeurosis.

questions.text: The ulnar nerve enters the forearm by passing between the two heads of origin of which muscle?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve enters the anterior forearm by passing through the cubital tunnel between the humeral and ulnar heads of flexor carpi ulnaris.

questions.text: Flexor carpi ulnaris inserts into which of the following structures?
options: Pisiform, hook of hamate, and base of 5th metacarpal
questions.correctAnswer: A. Pisiform, hook of hamate, and base of 5th metacarpal
questions.explanation: FCU inserts primarily into the pisiform, which anchors force onward to the hook of hamate and base of the 5th metacarpal.

questions.text: Which muscle constitutes the intermediate layer of the anterior forearm compartment?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Flexor digitorum superficialis
questions.explanation: Flexor digitorum superficialis sits between the superficial flexors and the deep layer (FDP, FPL, PQ), forming the intermediate layer.

questions.text: The tendons of the flexor digitorum superficialis split at the level of the proximal phalanges to allow passage of the tendons of:
questions.correctAnswer: B. Flexor digitorum profundus
questions.explanation: FDS tendons split (Camper's chiasm) over the proximal phalanx, allowing the deeper FDP tendons to pass through to the distal phalanges.

questions.text: Flexor digitorum superficialis tendons insert into the:
options: Sides of the middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5
Palmar plates of the MCP joints
questions.correctAnswer: B. Sides of the middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5
questions.explanation: The split slips of each FDS tendon reunite and insert onto the lateral borders of the middle phalanx of digits 2 through 5.

questions.text: Flexor digitorum profundus inserts into the:
options: Bases of the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5
questions.correctAnswer: B. Bases of the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5
questions.explanation: FDP tendons pass through the FDS splits to insert onto the palmar surfaces of the bases of the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5.

questions.text: Flexor digitorum profundus exhibits a dual nerve supply; which nerve supplies its medial half (digits 4 and 5)?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Ulnar nerve
questions.explanation: The medial half of FDP (controlling the ring and little fingers) is supplied directly by the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).

questions.text: The lateral half of the flexor digitorum profundus (digits 2 and 3) is innervated by the:
options: Anterior interosseous nerve (branch of median nerve)
questions.correctAnswer: B. Anterior interosseous nerve (branch of median nerve)
questions.explanation: The lateral half of FDP (controlling index and middle fingers) is innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the median nerve.

questions.text: Flexor pollicis longus originates primarily from the:
options: Anterior surface of the radius and adjacent interosseous membrane
questions.correctAnswer: B. Anterior surface of the radius and adjacent interosseous membrane
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis longus arises from the anterior surface of the radius between the tuberosity and pronator quadratus, and the interosseous membrane.

questions.text: Flexor pollicis longus inserts into the:
options: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
questions.correctAnswer: B. Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
questions.explanation: The tendon of FPL runs through the carpal tunnel to insert onto the palmar base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.

questions.text: Pronator quadratus originates from the:
options: Distal anterior shaft of the radius
Distal anterior shaft (lower 1/4) of the ulna
questions.correctAnswer: B. Distal anterior shaft (lower 1/4) of the ulna
questions.explanation: Pronator quadratus originates from the pronator ridge on the anterior surface of the lower fourth of the ulna and inserts into the lower fourth of the radius.

questions.text: Which muscle is the primary, initiating pronator of the forearm regardless of elbow angle?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Pronator quadratus
questions.explanation: Pronator quadratus initiates pronation consistently, whereas pronator teres adds power during rapid or resisted pronation.

questions.text: Both the flexor pollicis longus and pronator quadratus are innervated by the:
options: Anterior interosseous nerve (branch of median nerve)
Main trunk of the ulnar nerve
Deep branch of the radial nerve
questions.correctAnswer: A. Anterior interosseous nerve (branch of median nerve)
questions.explanation: The anterior interosseous nerve innervates FPL, pronator quadratus, and the lateral half of FDP.

questions.text: A laceration just proximal to the wrist dividing the flexor digitorum profundus tendon to the index finger causes complete loss of flexion at which joint:
questions.correctAnswer: C. Distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint
questions.explanation: Only the flexor digitorum profundus inserts into the distal phalanx, making it the sole flexor of the DIP joint.

questions.text: The common extensor tendon originates from which bony landmark?
options: Anterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus
questions.correctAnswer: B. Anterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus
questions.explanation: The superficial extensor muscles originate from the lateral epicondyle via the common extensor tendon.

questions.text: Which muscle arises from the upper two-thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Brachioradialis
questions.explanation: Brachioradialis originates from the proximal two-thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.

questions.text: Despite being anatomically in the posterior (extensor) compartment, brachioradialis functions as a:
options: Flexor of the elbow joint, particularly in the midprone position
questions.correctAnswer: B. Flexor of the elbow joint, particularly in the midprone position
questions.explanation: Crossing anterior to the elbow flexion axis, brachioradialis flexes the elbow with maximum mechanical efficiency in the midprone forearm position.

questions.text: Brachioradialis is innervated directly by the:
questions.correctAnswer: C. Radial nerve (prior to its bifurcation)
questions.explanation: Brachioradialis receives direct branches from the main trunk of the radial nerve in the arm prior to its bifurcation in the cubital fossa.

questions.text: Extensor carpi radialis longus inserts into the:
options: Dorsal aspect of the base of the 2nd metacarpal
Dorsal aspect of the base of the 3rd metacarpal
questions.correctAnswer: B. Dorsal aspect of the base of the 2nd metacarpal
questions.explanation: The tendon of ECRL inserts onto the dorsal surface of the base of the 2nd metacarpal.

questions.text: Extensor carpi radialis brevis inserts into the:
options: Dorsal surface of the base of the 3rd metacarpal
questions.correctAnswer: A. Dorsal surface of the base of the 3rd metacarpal
questions.explanation: ECRB originates from the common extensor origin and inserts onto the dorsal aspect of the base of the 3rd metacarpal.

questions.text: The posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve) pierces and traverses which muscle?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Supinator
questions.explanation: The deep branch of the radial nerve enters the posterior compartment by passing between the superficial and deep planes of the supinator muscle.

questions.text: The deep layer of the posterior forearm contains all of the following muscles EXCEPT:
questions.correctAnswer: C. Extensor digiti minimi
questions.explanation: Extensor digiti minimi belongs to the superficial extensor group; the deep outcropping muscles are supinator, APL, EPB, EPL, and extensor indicis.

questions.text: The extensor digitorum communis tendons form dorsal digital expansions (extensor hoods) over which fingers?
options: Medial four digits (index, middle, ring, little)
questions.correctAnswer: B. Medial four digits (index, middle, ring, little)
questions.explanation: Extensor digitorum divides into four tendons that form extensor expansions over the dorsal aspect of digits 2 through 5.

questions.text: Extensor carpi ulnaris inserts into the base of which bone?
questions.correctAnswer: C. Base of the 5th metacarpal
questions.explanation: Extensor carpi ulnaris inserts onto the medial tubercle on the base of the 5th metacarpal.

questions.text: The tendon of which muscle hooks acutely around Lister's tubercle (dorsal tubercle of the radius)?
questions.correctAnswer: C. Extensor pollicis longus
questions.explanation: Extensor pollicis longus hooks around the medial side of Lister's tubercle, utilizing it as a pulley to change direction toward the thumb.

questions.text: The lateral (radial) boundary of the anatomical snuffbox is formed by the tendons of:
options: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
questions.correctAnswer: B. Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
questions.explanation: The lateral/anterior border of the anatomical snuffbox is formed by the tendons of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis.

questions.text: The medial (ulnar) boundary of the anatomical snuffbox is formed by the tendon of:
questions.correctAnswer: C. Extensor pollicis longus
questions.explanation: The medial/posterior border of the anatomical snuffbox is formed exclusively by the tendon of extensor pollicis longus.

questions.text: Extensor pollicis longus inserts into the:
options: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
questions.correctAnswer: C. Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
questions.explanation: EPL extends to insert onto the dorsal aspect of the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.

questions.text: All muscles of the deep layer of the posterior forearm are innervated by the:
options: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
questions.correctAnswer: B. Posterior interosseous nerve (C7, C8)
questions.explanation: The posterior interosseous nerve supplies all muscles of the deep posterior forearm layer.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered a thenar muscle?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Abductor pollicis brevis
questions.explanation: The true thenar muscles are abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis, and opponens pollicis. Adductor pollicis lies in a separate fascial compartment.

questions.text: Abductor pollicis brevis originates from the flexor retinaculum and which carpal bones?
options: Tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium
questions.correctAnswer: B. Tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium
questions.explanation: APB arises from the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium and the flexor retinaculum.

questions.text: The thenar muscles are primarily innervated by which nerve?
options: Recurrent (motor) branch of the median nerve (C8, T1)
questions.correctAnswer: B. Recurrent (motor) branch of the median nerve (C8, T1)
questions.explanation: The recurrent branch of the median nerve supplies the thenar muscles; compression in carpal tunnel syndrome leads to thenar atrophy.

questions.text: The deep head of the flexor pollicis brevis is frequently innervated by the:
options: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
questions.correctAnswer: B. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis brevis typically has dual innervation: superficial head by the median nerve, and deep head by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

questions.text: Opponens pollicis inserts into which site?
options: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
Entire radial (lateral) border and anterior surface of the 1st metacarpal
Base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
questions.correctAnswer: B. Entire radial (lateral) border and anterior surface of the 1st metacarpal
questions.explanation: Opponens pollicis inserts along the lateral margin and palmar surface of the entire shaft of the 1st metacarpal to rotate it into opposition.

questions.text: Which muscle adducts the thumb toward the middle finger and is innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve?
questions.correctAnswer: C. Adductor pollicis
questions.explanation: Adductor pollicis adducts the thumb and is innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

questions.text: Adductor pollicis consists of two heads: oblique and transverse. The transverse head originates from the:
options: Anterior border of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal
questions.correctAnswer: B. Anterior border of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal
questions.explanation: The transverse head of adductor pollicis arises from the anterior ridge of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an intrinsic hypothenar muscle?
questions.correctAnswer: D. Palmar interosseous 1
questions.explanation: The hypothenar group consists of abductor digiti minimi, flexor digiti minimi brevis, and opponens digiti minimi.

questions.text: Abductor digiti minimi originates from the:
options: Pisiform bone and tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.correctAnswer: B. Pisiform bone and tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.explanation: Abductor digiti minimi originates from the pisiform and the tendon expansion of flexor carpi ulnaris.

questions.text: All hypothenar muscles are innervated by the:
options: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
questions.correctAnswer: B. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
questions.explanation: All intrinsic hypothenar muscles receive motor supply from the deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1).

questions.text: The lumbrical muscles originate from the tendons of which muscle in the palm?
questions.correctAnswer: B. Flexor digitorum profundus
questions.explanation: The four lumbricals arise directly from the four tendons of the flexor digitorum profundus in the palm.

questions.text: The 1st and 2nd lumbricals differ from the 3rd and 4th lumbricals because the 1st and 2nd are:
options: Unipennate and innervated by the median nerve
questions.correctAnswer: B. Unipennate and innervated by the median nerve
questions.explanation: The 1st and 2nd lumbricals are unipennate (arising from a single FDP tendon) and innervated by digital branches of the median nerve.

questions.text: The 3rd and 4th lumbricals are bipennate and innervated by the:
options: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
questions.correctAnswer: B. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
questions.explanation: The 3rd and 4th lumbricals arise from adjacent sides of two FDP tendons (bipennate) and are innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

questions.text: The lumbricals insert into the:
options: Lateral (radial) margins of the extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5
questions.correctAnswer: B. Lateral (radial) margins of the extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5
questions.explanation: Lumbricals pass anterior to the MCP joint and insert into the radial side of the dorsal digital expansion of their respective digits.

questions.text: The primary combined action of the lumbrical muscles is:
options: Extension of MCP and flexion of IP joints
Flexion of metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints and extension of interphalangeal (IP) joints
questions.correctAnswer: B. Flexion of metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints and extension of interphalangeal (IP) joints
questions.explanation: By crossing anterior to MCP joints and inserting into dorsal hoods, lumbricals flex the MCP joints and extend the interphalangeal joints.

questions.text: How many dorsal interossei muscles are present in each human hand?
questions.explanation: Each hand contains 4 bipennate dorsal interossei arising from the adjacent sides of the metacarpals.

questions.text: How many palmar interossei muscles are typically described in classical gross anatomy?
questions.correctAnswer: B. 3 (or 4 including rudimentary first)
questions.explanation: Classical gross anatomy describes 3 palmar interossei on digits 2, 4, and 5; when a rudimentary muscle to the thumb is counted, there are 4.

questions.text: Regarding the actions of the interossei, which mnemonic correctly summarizes their main movements?
questions.correctAnswer: A. DAB (Dorsal ABducts) and PAD (Palmar ADducts)
questions.explanation: Dorsal interossei ABduct digits relative to the 3rd digit (DAB), whereas palmar interossei ADduct digits toward the 3rd digit (PAD).

questions.text: The reference axis for abduction and adduction of the fingers by the interossei passes longitudinally through the:
questions.correctAnswer: B. Middle finger (3rd digit)
questions.explanation: Movement away from the longitudinal axis of the middle finger is abduction; movement toward it is adduction.

questions.text: All interossei (both dorsal and palmar) receive their motor innervation from the:
options: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1)
Superficial branch of the radial nerve
questions.correctAnswer: B. Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8, T1)
questions.explanation: Every interosseous muscle in the hand is supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
